Asobi 1.0.3 (build 2239) Nov 13, 2026

  • Swap a clip for another version. Right-click a clip in the playlist and choose Swap Version: its other versions beside it are listed newest first, or Choose a Version… picks any file. A file that doesn't look like a version of the clip asks before it goes in. Swap Every Clip to Its Latest Version brings a whole playlist up to date for a progress report. Each version keeps its own notes and drawings, and they come back if you swap back.
  • Relinking a moved conform finds it. A review of a conform movie that was moved into another folder lost every shot, even when you chose the right folder. It now finds the movie by itself. When it does need to ask, the window names what is missing and lets you pick the file as well as a folder.
  • Optimize keeps the app responsive. Checking the files before each encode no longer holds up the app, which could freeze it on a slow connection to the server or with a long playlist.
  • Slates keep the logo inside title safe. The Autonomy wordmark at the foot of a slate sat below the title-safe line.
Earlier updates

1.0.2 (build 2229) Nov 11, 2026

  • Web links show where they are. While a web link is being made, the line under the progress bar names the clip it is working on and the step: encoding the picture, packaging it for streaming, or uploading. The clip count is also right now; it used to read one ahead.

1.0.1 (build 2226) Nov 11, 2026

  • Check Frames finds repeated frames in movies too. A frame that repeats while the shot is moving is flagged in QuickTimes and MP4s as well as sequences, through H.264 and ProRes compression. A freeze or a hold isn't flagged, and a steady pattern, such as a frame-rate conversion, comes up as one row.
  • Vendor deliveries know where they came from. A clip from a job's 10_DELIVERIES vendor folders shows the vendor and the delivery day on its playlist row and in the notes report.
  • Compare with What We Sent. Right-click a vendor's clip to pair it with the plate we sent that vendor for its shot, from the delivery on or before theirs. Compare with Plate now finds the shot of a vendor clip too, and uses the sent plate when the shot's folders have none.
  • Vendor edits, shot by shot. After Find Shots and Match Shots on a vendor's edit movie, each shot pairs with its plate and starts on the plate's cut frame, as the pull recorded it.
  • The right take for a movie comp. Compare with Plate picks the plate whose timecode a QuickTime comp was made from, as it already did for EXR comps.
  • Push a grade in a live review. A new icon beside Copy and Paste grade sends this clip's grade to everyone, or puts it on every clip for everyone, in one step you can undo. Reviewers on Asobi Review who aren't expert reviewers ask the host first, and the host can allow them for the rest of the review.

1.0 (build 2215) Nov 10, 2026

  • Removing a clip in a live review removes it for everyone. When the host or anyone on a studio Mac takes a clip out of the playlist, it now leaves every other Asobi in the room and the web page too. Before, it stayed on everyone else's screen.
  • Update from Kitsu removes shots taken off the Kitsu playlist. Shots deleted from the Kitsu playlist now leave Asobi's playlist when you update, as one step you can undo. Clips you added yourself, and older versions of a shot that's still on the playlist, stay.

1.0 (build 2211) Nov 10, 2026

  • Showcases show what they're doing. Under "Preparing the picture" the Showcase window now says whether it is encoding the picture or packaging it for streaming, and the bar keeps moving through packaging. A long reel used to sit at halfway and look stuck.

1.0 (build 2208) Nov 9, 2026

  • Playlist actions on a right-click. The playlist's More menu could vanish the moment it opened. Its items (Import Timeline, Save As, Trim to In and Out, Clear Trim, Auto-Pair) are now in a Playlist section when you right-click the playlist's footer, a movie's header or any row.
  • Closing a floating panel brings it back. Closing a floating Notes, Playlist or Grade window puts it back in the side panel and shows it, instead of leaving it hidden behind another tab.

1.0 (build 2205) Nov 9, 2026

  • Menus that closed by themselves. Since 2199, menus and popovers in the window (the playlist's More, the color chip) could close the moment they opened, during playback or a busy review. Fixed. Edit ▸ Undo is plain "Undo" again; ⌘Z still takes back the last mark or playlist change.
  • Progress header. The Notes column's Progress view now reads "26 of 27 shots noted · 11 agency, Nov 8" and fits the column instead of being cut off.
  • Studio Tutorials: the Frame.io round with the agency now has step-by-step figures.

1.0 (build 2199) Nov 9, 2026

  • As on this Mac. A new first choice in the color chip's Footage menu: Asobi leaves the color alone and the picture looks as it does in Preview or QuickTime Player. Stills, and movies from outside the shot folders that nobody has set a color for, start this way.
  • Rejoining a big review. A Mac could fail to join or rejoin a review with a lot in it ("Message too long") while the browser joined fine. Fixed.
  • Sort ▸ Cut Order. Puts every cut movie's shots back together in the edit's order. The shots of one cut can no longer be unlinked from each other.
  • Undo for the playlist. ⌘Z takes back the last playlist change as well as the last mark: adding, removing, moving, sorting, pairing, linking, Set Kitsu Shots, split, join and rename. Edit ▸ Undo says which.
  • Dragging in the playlist. Hold a clip over a row to pair them; a drag that only passes over rows moves the clip, and says where it will land.
  • A new studio tutorial: a round with the agency on Frame.io, for coordinators and producers.
